questions.question: In your own words, state Newton's Second Law of Motion.
questions.expected_answer: When a net force acts on an object, the object will accelerate in the direction of the net force. The acceleration is directly proportional to the net force and inversely proportional to the mass.

questions.question: Why is it important to identify the *net* force rather than just any force when calculating acceleration?
questions.expected_answer: Because an object might have multiple forces acting on it. It's the combined, resultant (net) effect of all those forces that actually causes the object's acceleration, not just one individual force.

questions.question: If you double the mass of an object but keep the net force the same, what happens to its acceleration?
questions.expected_answer: The acceleration will be halved, because acceleration is inversely proportional to mass.
